constraints: Regulations: FIA Sporting Regulations edition 2025-i5 (the issue in force on the race date).
Art. 54.3 / 54.4(c): pending 5s time penalty. At the next stop the car must be stationary for 5s before anyone touches it (+5.0s to the stop); with no further stop it is added to race time.

hits.query: serving a 5 second time penalty at a pit stop, the car may not be worked on until stationary
hits.text:
54.4 c) Whilst a car is stationary in the pit lane as a result of incurring a penalty in accordance
with Articles 54.3a) or 54.3b) above, it may not be worked on until the car has been
stationary for the duration of the penalty. In this context, touching the car or driver by
hand or tools or equipment will all constitute working.

hits.citation: 2024 Austrian GP: Norris 5 s penalty for track limits
hits.query: serving a 5 second time penalty at a pit stop, the car may not be worked on until stationary
hits.text: 2024 Austrian Grand Prix, car 4 (NOR). Lap 61: incident under investigation for track limits. Lap 64: 5 second time penalty for track limits. A 5 second time penalty is served as a stationary hold at the next pit stop or, if the driver does not stop again, added to his race time.

hits.query: serving a 5 second time penalty at a pit stop, the car may not be worked on until stationary
hits.text:
54.4 d) Whilst a car is stationary in the pit lane as a result of incurring a time penalty in accordance
with Article 54.3d) above it may not be worked on. However, if the engine stops any work
necessary to re-start it may be carried out after the time penalty period has elapsed. If
the Competitor is unable to start the engine the car may then only be worked on in the
driver's garage.
